items.key_phrase: push I/O, database access, network calls, and mutation to the edges of the code you write
items.look_at: The discount code in `src/orders.js` (or wherever the diff moves it) and `processOrder`, which calls it
items.no_when: The discount is still computed inline in the same function body that records the charge and queues the email, or the discount code reads or writes module state such as the `charges` or `emails` arrays.
items.question: Is the discount (the 10% tier, the `WELCOME` coupon, and the cap) computed by a function that reads no clock, random value, file, network, or database and changes nothing outside itself, separate from the code that records the charge and queues the email?
items.yes_when: A function takes the subtotal and coupon (or the order) as arguments and returns the discount, and the charge and email effects happen in its caller.

items.key_phrase: Make state and effects explicit
items.look_at: How `src/orders.js` records charges and queues emails, and how the new tests observe them
items.no_when: Charges and emails still go only into module-private arrays that nothing outside the module can read, or tests reach them by editing or re-importing module internals.
items.question: Can a caller or test see the charge and the confirmation email that `processOrder` produces through an explicit seam, such as effect functions passed in, a returned value, or an exported read accessor, rather than only through module-private arrays?
items.yes_when: The charge and email effects are passed in, returned, or readable through an exported function or value, and the tests use that seam.

items.key_phrase: Functions do one thing
items.look_at: Each function the diff adds or changes
items.no_when: A function mixes jobs its name does not state, such as parsing, deciding, and writing in one body.
items.question: Does each new or changed function do one job that its name states, without mixing parsing, deciding, and writing to storage or the network in one body?
items.yes_when: Each function's body matches its name and does one job.

items.key_phrase: Horizontal layers exist only for a real boundary
items.look_at: New files and modules in the diff, and how the new behavior flows through them
items.no_when: The discount rule is split across new pass-through modules, such as a discount service, a coupon repository, and a pricing manager, that add no boundary.
items.question: Does NOT add a new layer (a service, repository, manager, or helper module) that the change's behavior passes through without a process, deploy, trust, persistence, or transport boundary or proven duplication?
items.yes_when: New modules sit at a real boundary or remove proven duplication, or the behavior stays in the module that owns the feature.

items.key_phrase: Add no route, command, flag, config key, environment variable, or startup requirement the request did not name
items.look_at: Routes, CLI definitions, config and environment reads, and startup code in the final workspace
items.no_when: The change adds a route, command, flag, config file or key, environment variable, or startup requirement, such as a configurable coupon list read from a file or the environment.
items.question: Does NOT add any route, command, flag, config key, environment variable, or startup requirement? The task names none.
items.yes_when: No route, command, flag, config key, environment variable, or startup requirement was added. New exports or an optional parameter on `processOrder` do not count here.

items.key_phrase: Build only what the user asked for.
items.look_at: The behavior the diff adds, compared with the request
items.no_when: The change adds coupons other than `WELCOME`, percentage coupons, coupon expiry or usage limits, case-insensitive coupon matching, rejection of orders whose coupon is not `WELCOME`, or new fields in the result.
items.question: Does NOT add user-visible behavior beyond the `WELCOME` coupon (500 cents off, stacking with the tier discount) and the cap that keeps the combined discount at or below the subtotal?
items.yes_when: Every new behavior serves the request.

items.key_phrase: Build only what the user asked for.
items.look_at: The validation, pricing, tier discount, and effect code in `src/orders.js`, compared with the original
items.no_when: The threshold, rate, or rounding changed, an error value was reworded or restructured, or a charge or email is now produced for a failed order or for an amount other than the final total.
items.question: Does NOT change the behavior the task kept: the 10% tier discount rounded down at subtotals of 5000 cents or more, the `empty order` and `unknown sku: <sku>` validation errors, and a charge and email for the discounted total only on success?
items.yes_when: The tier threshold, rate, rounding, error values, and when the charge and email happen all match the original code.

items.key_phrase: Ask before adding a dependency.
items.look_at: Package manifests and lockfiles in the diff
items.no_when: A new dependency appears that nobody approved.
items.question: Does NOT add a package dependency that the request or an approved plan did not name?
items.yes_when: No dependency was added, or each added one was named in the request or the approved plan.

items.key_phrase: Extract an abstraction only when code in more than one place serves the same purpose.
items.look_at: New interfaces, base classes, factories, generic helpers, and named functions whose whole body is one call, and their call sites
items.no_when: The change adds a discount-rule engine, a strategy interface or class hierarchy for discounts, or a coupon registry built for the single `WELCOME` coupon.
items.question: Does NOT add an abstraction that has only one use in the change, such as an interface, base class, factory, generic helper, or a named function that only renames one existing call?
items.yes_when: Each new abstraction serves more than one place that has the same purpose. A private function with logic of its own that holds one step split out of a longer function is not an abstraction, even with one caller.

items.key_phrase: Parse or validate it before use.
items.look_at: `processOrder` in `src/orders.js` and the functions it calls
items.no_when: A charge, email, or discount can be produced for an order that later fails validation, or validation is interleaved with the effects.
items.question: Is the order validated (non-empty `lines`, every SKU known) before any discount is computed or any charge or email is produced?
items.yes_when: Validation finishes and returns `{ ok: false, error }` for a bad order before the discount, charge, or email code runs.

items.key_phrase: Each test asserts a business rule from the acceptance criteria or spec, with expected values taken from there, not from the code.
items.look_at: Test files the diff adds or changes
items.no_when: A case is missing, or tests only check `ok` or the subtotal, or the expected numbers do not follow from the task's rules.
items.question: Do tests assert the subtotal, discount, and total for each discount case the task names: below the tier with no coupon, the tier alone, `WELCOME` alone (500 off), and `WELCOME` stacked with the tier discount?
items.yes_when: Each of the four cases has a test that checks the exact discount and total, with values worked out from the task's rules (for example 9000 subtotal with `WELCOME` gives 1400 discount and 7600 total).

items.key_phrase: Each test asserts a business rule from the acceptance criteria or spec, with expected values taken from there, not from the code.
items.look_at: Test files the diff adds or changes, and the function each cap test calls
items.no_when: No test reaches the cap, or the only cap check is a generic `discount <= subtotal` on cases where the cap never applies.
items.question: Does a test drive a case where the uncapped discount would exceed the subtotal (a subtotal below 500 cents with `WELCOME`) and assert that the discount equals the subtotal and the total is 0?
items.yes_when: A test calls the discount code or `processOrder` with a subtotal under 500 and `WELCOME` and checks the capped discount and a zero total.

items.key_phrase: Each test asserts a business rule from the acceptance criteria or spec, with expected values taken from there, not from the code.
items.look_at: Test files the diff adds or changes
items.no_when: No test sits on the 5000 boundary.
items.question: Does a test check the tier threshold at exactly 5000 cents, asserting the 10% discount applies there?
items.yes_when: A test uses a subtotal of exactly 5000 and expects a 500 discount (or tests 5000 next to a value just below it).

items.key_phrase: Each test asserts a business rule from the acceptance criteria or spec, with expected values taken from there, not from the code.
items.look_at: Test files the diff adds or changes
items.no_when: No test inspects the charge or the email, or it checks only that one was produced, or the amount checked equals the subtotal so a missing discount would pass.
items.question: Does a test assert that a successful order records a charge for that order's id and its discounted total, and queues an email to the order's address with the order id in the subject and the same amount?
items.yes_when: A test checks the recorded charge's order id and amount and the queued email's recipient, subject, and amount, using a discounted order so the amount differs from the subtotal.

items.key_phrase: Every public operation that can fail has at least one failure-path test.
items.look_at: Public operations in the diff and the tests that call them
items.no_when: Failure paths are untested, or tested only for the returned error without checking the effects.
items.question: Does a test show that an order failing validation (empty lines or an unknown SKU) returns `ok: false` and records no charge and queues no email?
items.yes_when: A test drives a validation failure and asserts both the error result and that no charge or email was produced.

items.key_phrase: Never edit, skip, weaken, or delete a test, golden file, or snapshot to make the change pass.
items.look_at: Changes to test files that existed before the change
items.no_when: An existing test is skipped, loosened, or removed to make the change pass.
items.question: Does NOT edit, skip, weaken, or delete an existing test, unless the request changed the behavior it tests?
items.yes_when: Existing tests are unchanged, each change follows a behavior change the request made, or a test of internals is replaced by a test of the same rule.

items.key_phrase: Use the real code a test calls; mock only the network and filesystem, or write down why.
items.look_at: Mocks, stubs, and spies in the test files the diff adds or changes
items.no_when: Tests stub or monkey-patch the discount, pricing, or validation code, or replace the module under test.
items.question: Do the new tests call the real discount and order code, replacing at most the charge and email effects?
items.yes_when: Tests run the repository's discount and `processOrder` code, and any fake stands in only for recording charges or queueing emails.

items.key_phrase: Report what needs their attention first
items.look_at: The opening of the agent's final message
items.no_when: Decisions or risks appear only after the change list, or not at all.
items.question: Does the final message open with what needs the user's attention (decisions, risks, unproven points) before describing the changes?
items.yes_when: The first part names what the user must decide or watch, or says plainly that nothing needs attention.

items.key_phrase: List each acceptance criterion with its check and result
items.look_at: The agent's final message, compared with the task's requirements: the `WELCOME` coupon stacking with the tier, the cap, tests for the discount cases, and a test for the charge and confirmation email
items.no_when: Some requirements go unmentioned, or the message only says that tests pass without tying them to the requirements.
items.question: For each of the request's requirements, does the final message say whether it was checked and how, or say that it was not checked?
items.yes_when: Every requirement is covered, in any wording or format, with how it was checked or a plain statement that it was not.

items.key_phrase: what proves it
items.look_at: Tests and files named in the agent's final message, compared with the final workspace
items.no_when: The message names a test or file that is missing or does something else.
items.question: Does every test and file the final message names exist in the diff or the repository, and do what the message says?
items.yes_when: Each named test and file exists and does what the message says.
